sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Complex Historical Context
sections.description: The patient presenting for this case report is a male in his late 70s whose clinical trajectory exemplifies the escalating complexity of "lifetime" management in structural heart disease. Upon admission to the Academician E.I. Chazov National Medical Research Center, he presented with classic symptoms of advanced aortic stenosis and heart failure, specifically exertional dyspnea, dizziness, and fatigue. Notably, he described a distinct spastic sensation in the left side of the chest during physical exertion, limiting his walking distance to approximately 200–300 meters. These symptoms signaled a critical hemodynamic compromise that necessitated immediate reassessment of his valvular status. sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Sequential Structural Valve Deterioration
sections.description: The failure of a transcatheter aortic valve in a "TAV-in-TAV" or "TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV" scenario represents a convergence of distinct pathological processes that differ significantly from the natural history of native valve disease or isolated surgical valve replacement. In the case presented, the patient's final intervention addressed a complex interplay of standard structural valve deterioration (SVD), the mechanical constraints imposed by multiple overlapping stent frames, and sequelae of prior infective endocarditis. Understanding these mechanisms is critical for appreciating why each successive reintervention presents escalating technical hurdles and why the physiological reserve required to tolerate them diminishes rapidly.
subtopics: Pathophysiology of Sequential Structural Valve Deterioration
